newsitem.title: USA: Computer show to highlight new network products.
newsitem.headline: Computer show to highlight new network products.

text.p: The Internet community puts itself on show and its boldest claims to the test in Las Vegas this week at Networld+Interop, the computer network industry's semiannual display of new products and strategies.

Now nearly a decade old, Networld+Interop started because Internet pioneers in industry, at universities and in government wanted to open communications as much as possible on the global computer network, a challenge since it has been built with equipment and software from rival suppliers.
But in growing to accommodate the burgeoning business of linking computers into networks, Networld has outgrown its original experimental ethic to become the industry's premier trade show.
Thousands of industry officials and computer users will descend on the show, and boasting rights, as well as billions of dollars in potential new contracts, will be at stake.

"As networking has grown up to be more of a business, Networld has become more mainstream," said John Gallant, a show veteran and editor-in-chief of Network World, a leading magazine covering the industry.
"It used to be more of an insiders show, attracting all the people who were religious about networking," he said.

From this initial vision of making the Internet as wide open as possible has grown a show expected to attract 650 equipment suppliers and 50,000 people, mainly corporate buyers planning their own organizational networks.
More than 200 miles of copper phone wire and 140 miles of fiber optic cable have been spliced together to create the show's massive electronic exhibits.

On view will be the latest equipment for handling high-speed transmission of computer data, phone-quality voice and real-time video images over networks of all types, from local area networks to massive phone company installations.
Also on display will be equipment aimed at easing the Internet's growing pains -- traffic bottlenecks that slow communication and threaten to bring the new communications medium screeching to a halt.
Products designed to build intranets, the internal corporate networks that are built according to Internet standards, will be another major theme.

Other technologies hoping to attract attention include wireless network, enhanced Internet software security systems and new methods for "pushing," or essentially broadcasting, specific information over networks to computer users.
Major announcements have been promised from Bay Networks Inc. and Northern Telecom Ltd., among others.

Dozens of new products than can send data at billions of bits a second -- so-called gigabit speed -- over local area networks will be shown along with new technologies that allow fast transmission over phone lines. That is far faster than current speeds and could allow transmission of live video and other images that gobble up huge amounts of data.

At a news conference and a keynote speech on Tuesday, David House, the recently hired chief executive at troubled Bay Networks, was expected to announce his strategy and product roadmap for turning the company around.
House was expected to announce a slew of new products to answer customer concerns that the company has failed to keep up with faster-growing rivals in several key technology areas.
Northern Telecom Ltd, Canada's big telecom equipment supplier, plans to announce a series of moves to raise its profile as a leading corporate data network supplier.

William Conner, a marketing vice president at Nortel's Enterprise Networks group, said the group will unveil plans to weave together its diversified businesses and compete more keenly with Cisco Systems Inc. and other companies.
"There's a new world ahead in the communications industry and we are going to play head-to-head across that network," Conner said.
